claims.text: A refractory high-entropy alloy containing multiple refractory elements such as Mo, Nb, Ta, and W can be an effective HER/HOR electrocatalyst.
The proposed RHEA provides a highly stable and corrosion-resistant surface.
The proposed RHEA has an electronically heterogeneous surface.
Its heterogeneous surface promotes favorable hydrogen adsorption and desorption kinetics.
The proposed initial RHEA is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Arc melting or sputtering can produce the proposed RHEA.
The synthesized RHEA exhibits atomic-scale chemical disorder and a fine-grained structure.
Atomic-level chemical disorder, fine grain boundaries, and possible interstitial effects create a broad distribution of catalytic active sites.
The multi-element composition produces a range of hydrogen-binding energies.
The distribution of binding energies supplies sites that bind hydrogen neither too strongly nor too weakly.
Strong interatomic bonds and lattice distortion impart corrosion resistance and structural stability under reactive conditions.
The combination of favorable hydrogen binding and structural stability enhances both catalytic activity and long-term durability.
The RHEA will exhibit lower HER/HOR overpotentials than conventional monometallic or binary catalysts.
The RHEA will exhibit higher HER/HOR exchange current densities than conventional monometallic or binary catalysts.
The RHEA will show reduced performance degradation during electrochemical cycling.
The proposed benefits are expected to be most pronounced when catalyst corrosion resistance and mechanical stability are critical.
The catalytic activity depends on surface area and electrical conductivity.
Direct evidence connecting refractory HEA compositions to enhanced HER/HOR electrocatalysis is limited.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome claims lower overpotential than conventional catalysts, whereas the falsification rule accepts merely comparable overpotential to Pt if durability improves. Thus, the experiment can count as successful without confirming the stated activity enhancement.
